interpretation: The candidate-count rule is not a stable proxy for dominant QRS polarity: it disagrees with the median-prominence rule on 20/48 records.
Record 207, the known catastrophic polarity failure, is selected positive by the current rule but negative by the signal-only prominence rule.
Record 108 is also selected negative by the signal-only prominence rule despite the current rule selecting positive.
Record 232 remains positive under both rules, indicating polarity selection is not the sole explanation for that failure.
No annotation information was used to choose any experimental polarity decision.
This report is diagnostic only; it must not replace or revise the locked 75-ms benchmark.
next_experiment: Run the prominence-based selector as a preregistered secondary detector on the same full MIT-BIH set and compare against the frozen baseline; do not select the winner using the same test set.
